correctness.rationale: The combinatorial Laplacian decomposes exactly into constant symmetric/antisymmetric eigenspaces of eigenvalues 0 and 2n-2 and two (n-1)-dimensional zero-sum pair eigenspaces at n and n-2. For n>=3 these are distinct; by PBH an installed coordinate set is controllable precisely when >=n-1 matched pair labels are represented. Loss of two pair labels is the sole obstruction, making the minimum adversarial channel cut c_(1)+c_(2). For iid failure probability 0<p<1, each single/double pair is nonempty with probability respectively s=1-p and r=1-p²; summing events of zero or one empty pair gives the exact all-budget formula. Against a placement with one originally empty pair, the full-coverage reliability advantage is r^a s^{b-2}[p s(b-2)+a p² s²/r]>0 in every feasible n>=3 case. Independently enumerated all placements and rational failure outcomes for n=3..5, 54 budget/failure-probability cases, verifying formulas and all optimal profiles. Infinite assertions rest on eigenspaces and strict algebra, not finite testing.

originality.rationale: Important strong overlap: the published November 2 weighted complete-bipartite perfect-matching-detuning theorem already gives the general PBH rank formula and the >=n-1 pair-index criterion for all t>0 with t!=1. Its proof extends essentially without change to t=0 crown graphs, so the base controllability criterion, matching-pair pattern and crown spectrum are NOT claimed independently new. The independently assessed surviving finding is the complete sharp adversarial tolerance cutoffs and ALL installation-budget iid failure reliability and optimizer classifications on the actual t=0 crown; the source rank theorem does not supply these stochastic and robust extremal laws, and the more general 2026 actuator-selection framework gives methods but not this closed graph-family law. Best-of-knowledge originality is limited to this robust/reliability result, with a significant deduction-priority risk.
residual_risks: Strong prior overlap: the entire base control criterion is a routine boundary specialization of a more general published weighted-graph rank theorem.
Optimal reliability formula is an elementary consequence of pair-coverage plus Bernoulli independence and may be independently published as a network reliability result under alternate terminology.
No results for unequal/correlated failures, weighted crowns, or general jointly designed inputs.

value.rationale: The natural design problem of reliable coordinate actuation after stochastic and worst-case channel loss is quantitatively different from merely testing fixed-graph controllability. The complete all-budget probability optimum and exact zero-through-three-fault installation minima identify all optimal placements for every n and 0<p<1, sharply changing from n to 2n-1 installed channels between one- and two-fault robustness. Although the eigenspace and counting algebra is short once the known rank structure is available, the natural robust-control benchmark and exact all-parameter optimal-placement classification are independently useful and not an arbitrary finite slice.

limitations: No weighting, heterogeneous or correlated failures, or arbitrary actuation vector design.
Strong previously published fixed-PBH coverage sharply limits the novelty scope.
